subject: EdgePrint renewal — usage pattern and expansion discussion
messages:
From: Tanya Wu <tanya.wu@edgeprint.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: EdgePrint renewal — usage pattern & expansion ask

Hi Rafael,

Quick note as we start renewal planning for EdgePrint. Over the last six weeks our real-time inference traffic spiked ~30% on tail queries and our batch embedding pipelines doubled in peak concurrency. We expect this pattern to continue as we onboard two new retail customers in Q2.

We’re approaching renewal (contract under DEAL-7842) and would like to explore options to avoid token throttles during peak windows. Specifically: can we add a modest committed GPU tranche and keep a small burst pool for unpredictable spikes? If so, what sizing do you recommend based on our usage? I attached a sanitized usage export for the past 60 days.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call next week to align on a sizing recommendation and a mutual action plan (M.A.P) for the renewal?

Thanks,
Tanya
Tanya Wu
Head of Platform Ops, EdgePrint AI
attachments: usage_export_Mar2028.csv (csv, 2.3MB)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Wu <tanya.wu@edgeprint.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Mar 2028 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgePrint renewal — usage pattern & expansion ask

Hi Tanya — thanks for the data and the heads-up.

We’ll run a short utilization audit and propose two concrete paths:
- Option A (steady commit): add a committed H100 tranche sized to cover 95th percentile sustained throughput; lower per-token unit cost; small ramp required at contract sign.
- Option B (hybrid burst): modest commit + 20–30% burst pool (on-demand H100) for short peaks; preserves SLAs but reduces upfront spend.

Before the call, is it OK if we instrument a 30-day log pull and perform a KV-cache/sequence-length sensitivity analysis? That will let us quantify tail latency and expected QoS gains for each path. If you’re OK I’ll include Karthik (capacity modeling) and Vanessa (pricing & commercial) on the MAP.

Proposed times for a 30-minute sync: Tue 3/14 10:00am PT or Wed 3/15 2:00pm PT. Which works?

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: EdgePrint renewal — sizing recommendation (proposal v1)

Team —

Recap: EdgePrint (DEAL-7842) saw a ~30% recent spike in tail traffic and ~2x peak batch concurrency. They approved a 30-day read-only log pull. Attached is a first-pass sizing proposal (sizing_proposal_v1.pdf). High-level recommendation follows:

1) Recommended configuration (preferred: hybrid burst):
   - Commit: 8 H100 equivalent slots (covers ~85% of peak 95th-percentile sustained load after KV-cache and batching improvements)
   - Burst pool: 3 H100 on-demand seats (short-duration spikes)
   - Autoscale policy: aggressive prefix cache hits trigger batch consolidation; emergency fallback to lower-cost model variant for non-critical batch jobs

2) Rationale:
   - Usage audit projects headroom gap of ~28% against current commit at 95th percentile when accounting for sequence-length distribution and cold-starts.
   - Hybrid reduces their expected monthly $/token by ~12% vs full on-demand, while keeping <300ms tail latency target for production gen.

3) Commercials & ops:
   - Pricing: commit discount tier at 12% off list for H100 tranche; burst consumption billed at on-demand rate.
   - Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing per EdgePrint request (finance prefers this).
   - SLA: committed tranche backed by 99.5% availability; burst best-effort with warm standby.

4) Next steps (internal):
   - Karthik: finalize capacity model and expected utilization curve + safe margin (ETA 3/17).
   - Ben: draft MAP language (scope, timings, rollback, credits) and optional A/B canary plan (ETA 3/18).
   - Vanessa: prepare commercial term sheet with quarterly billing option and updated discount band (ETA 3/17).

I’ll send this to Tanya after we confirm the numbers. If we land on Option A (steady commit), we’ll propose 12 H100 equivalents with a 6-week ramp.

Cheers,
Rafael
attachments: sizing_proposal_v1.pdf (pdf, 210KB)
